name: Ibn al-Wardi
bio: Zayn al-Din Umar ibn al-Muzaffar ibn al-Wardi was a poet, man of letters, historian and Shafi'i jurist, born in Ma'arrat al-Nu'man in 691 AH (1292 CE). He served as judge at Manbij and lived in Aleppo. His works include a diwan, a continuation of Abu al-Fida's history known as the History of Ibn al-Wardi, a versification of a Shafi'i law manual, maqamas, and books on grammar, and he exchanged poems of rivalry with Salah al-Din al-Safadi. The Lamiyya beginning “Leave off the talk of songs and love poetry” is attributed to him, though it was not in his diwan and was added to its printed edition. He died in Aleppo in the plague of 749 AH (1349 CE), soon after writing a maqama about it.
